title: XSS Detection: Path-Component Injection and Error Page Reflection
goal: The current xss_extended runner only tests XSS in query parameters and known form inputs. It does NOT inject payloads into URL path segments. Gruyere's first (and most obvious) vulnerability is reflected XSS in the error page: requesting /[instance-id]/INVALID_PATH reflects the path component unescaped in the error HTML. This is never detected because no runner tries path-based XSS. Add path-component XSS testing to xss_extended: for each discovered base URL like https://example.com/app/, append XSS payloads as path segments (https://example.com/app/<script>alert(1)</script>) and check if the payload appears unescaped in the response HTML. Also add error-page reflection detection: try 5 common invalid paths (/notexist, /404test, /error, /undefined, /<payload>) and check if any URL-component is reflected in the response body without HTML encoding.
generation_reason: Gruyere's most obvious vulnerability (reflected XSS in error page via path segment injection) is completely undetected because xss_extended only tests query parameters. No runner tries /base/<script>alert(1)</script>.

implementation_notes.test_approach: For each base_target, construct: base_target + '/' + url_encoded_payload. Send GET request. Check if raw payload or decoded form appears in response.text without HTML entity encoding.
implementation_notes.detection_logic: If payload_text in response.text OR unescaped_html_entities(payload_text) in response.text → finding. Check: <, >, ', " are NOT encoded in the response.
implementation_notes.error_page_approach: Also try 3 random invalid paths (/aegispt-404-test, /undefined-path-xss-probe, /error-test) and check if any URL component appears reflected. If so, test with XSS payload.
